Your first move starts the story.

Control is a map of attacks and defenses. It is not a position score.

Reading the board

A piece controls the squares it attacks, including squares occupied by its own pieces. A pawn controls its two forward diagonals, not the square it moves into.

Bishops, rooks, and queens stop at the first piece along each line. Knights jump. Kings control their adjacent squares. Pinned pieces still count as controlling squares, even when moving would expose their king.

Teal: White Coral: Black Stripes: both

Each side's percentage uses all 64 squares. Shared squares count for both sides, so the percentages do not need to add to 100%.

Select a piece to outline its reach. Dots show legal destinations for the side to move. Hover or focus a square to see its attackers. Play both sides, or use move history to revisit a position. Playing from an earlier position replaces the later moves.

Your game is saved in this browser. No chess engine or move evaluations are used.
